references.title: Adaptive backward Euler time stepping with truncation error control for numerical modelling of unsaturated fluid flow
references.journal: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering
references.relevance: Embedded backward-Euler/Thomas-Gladwell derivative formulation; first- and second-order estimates can share a nonlinear system/derivative construction at minimal additional storage/cost in the published formulation.

references.title: Noniterative time stepping schemes with adaptive truncation error control for the solution of Richards equation
references.relevance: Derivative-predicted nonlinear coefficients followed by a single correction are a bounded-cost direction; the paper also states that intrinsically mass-conservative/chord-slope formulations complicate the formal second-order construction.

embedded_pair_identity.conclusion: The F-SI23 raw derivative-difference observer is algebraically the BE-versus-TG embedded output difference when both estimates share compatible derivative history. It is not a separate independent error oracle.
embedded_pair_identity.SWAP_principal_state_rule: h_TG must not replace the mass-conservative principal BE candidate in F-SI24. Any companion is decision-only until independently qualified.

single_linear_mode_analysis.interpretation: The raw BE/TG observer is asymptotically accurate for nonstiff/small-x modes but can become grossly conservative for strongly damped stiff modes. This analytically explains why F-SI23 C2/C3 can show very large raw observer ratios after a prescribed-head discontinuity without invalidating the exact small-step eigenmode relation.

effective_scalar_stiffness_diagnostic.pure_mode_identity: If udot_n and udot_np1 are nonzero, same-sign derivatives of one scalar linear mode, x=udot_n/udot_np1-1 exactly.
generic_vector_limitation: A Richards column contains multiple spatial modes/eigenvalues, so one component derivative ratio is generally a mixture of modes.
Derivative components may be zero, cross zero, change sign or be dominated by different modes at different nodes/times.
Using the bottom-node derivative ratio as a universal column stiffness number has no general source/theory guarantee.
F-SI23 C3 already showed non-monotone finite-comparator ratios during retry halving before the late decreasing regime.

stored_jacobian_reuse.reason: Current HeadCalc dfdh arrays are assembled at old_head before the final accepted Newton update and are not rebuilt after convergence.
stored_jacobian_reuse.allowed_future_use: A lagged operator could only be reconsidered after independently bounding the iterate-lag effect; F-SI24 Gate A makes no such assumption.

posthoc_single_resolvent_filter.reason: A generic expression such as applying one final-state Jacobian inverse to e_h is not by itself a derived stiff local-error estimator. The required right-hand side/operator scaling must be derived from the semi-discrete equations; an arbitrary resolvent filter would be an empirical numerical policy change.

literature_backed_single_correction_comp.shape: Use accepted/committed derivative information to predict the nonlinear coefficient evaluation state and perform exactly one solver-owned linear correction under a source-bound semi-discrete operator, producing a decision-only embedded companion while leaving the principal mixed-form BE state unchanged.
literature_backed_single_correction_comp.expected_extra_storage: O(N) worker scratch plus already-required optional derivative history
literature_backed_single_correction_comp.literature_support: The 2002 noniterative Richards work explicitly identifies time-derivative prediction followed by a single correction as the key bounded-cost strategy.
literature_backed_single_correction_comp.mass_rule: The companion never replaces the principal state and never weakens the independent hard mass gate.
remaining_derivation_questions: Which SWAP semi-discrete state/operator is predicted: pressure-form coefficients, mixed-form chord-slope storage operator, or a decision-only pressure-head linearization?
How is the prediction formed at initialization/restart/right-side boundary discontinuity without reusing an incompatible left derivative?
What exact companion difference is used as the scalar/vector indicator and what order/reliability statement is valid for SWAP's mixed-form storage treatment?
Can the restricted SwKimpl=0 final/predicted operator be obtained through a clean solver-owned interface without duplicating HeadCalc internals?
Does the construction remain robust when the derivative contains multiple stiff spatial modes?

next_action: Freeze a Gate-B formulation contract for the derivative-predicted single-correction companion. It must specify the exact semi-discrete equations, predictor state, linear operator, right-hand side, discontinuity bootstrap semantics, companion output and failure/unavailability semantics before any executable test is written.
